extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of literature/humour interested in the nature and forms of wit
extracted.subtask_description: Describe and identify the characteristics, forms, and uses of wit as a literary and conversational form of intelligent humour. Suitable for readers seeking conceptual definitions and distinctions (quip, repartee, witticism, metaphysical wit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as intelligent humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is a form of intelligent humour — the ability to say or write things that are clever and typically funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Someone witty (a wit) is skilled at wit; this definition centers cleverness and typical funniness as the core qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Making spontaneous one-line or single-phrase jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasizes spontaneity and short, pithy expressions (one-line/single-phrase) as characteristic of much wit (e.g., repartee, quips).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repartee (quick answer and capping comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repartee is the wit of the quick answer and capping comment: the snappy comeback and neat retort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued for speed and conversational timing; repartee functions as a rapid exchange rather than extended argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quip characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: A quip is an observation or saying that has some wit but perhaps descends into sarcasm, or otherwise is short of a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quips may trade clarity or seriousness for a sharp or sarcastic turn; they can be witty yet less substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witticism as diminutive
rubrics_metrics.description: A witticism also suggests the diminutive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames certain witty remarks as smaller, lighter or less ambitious forms of wit (brief playful comments rather than sustained cleverness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingeniousness vs laugh-out-loud humour (and potential cruelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Witty remarks may be intentionally cruel (as also in many epigrams), and perhaps more ingenious than funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wit can prioritize cleverness, sharpness, or sting over eliciting laughter; historical examples (e.g., Dorothy Parker/Algonquin Round Table) show wit that can offend or be cutting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordplay combined with conceptual thinking (metaphysical wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: It may combine word play with conceptual thinking, as a kind of verbal display requiring attention, without intending to be laugh-out-loud funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen especially in metaphysical poetry (e.g., John Donne); such wit rewards intellectual engagement and can disguise more poignant feelings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of wit (quip, repartee, wisecrack)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of wit include the quip, repartee, and wisecrack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these labels to classify instances of wit: quip (brief observation), repartee (quick comeback), wisecrack (sharp, often flippant remark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader senses and idioms of 'wits'
rubrics_metrics.description: More generally, one's wits are one's intellectual powers of all types (native wit = common sense; to have one's wits about one = alert and capable of quick reasoning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These idiomatic uses are non-comedic but related to cognitive agility underlying wit; useful for distinguishing rhetorical/lexical senses from the humourous form.
